state.case_summary:
A young black woman with sickle cell disease (HbSS variant) presented with a 2-day history of visual loss in the left eye. No dehydration or other precipitating factors were noted.

Visual acuity was 20/20 OD and 20/800 OS. Right eye examination was unremarkable except for peripheral retinal black sunburst lesions. In her left eye, ischemic macular whitening was noted. No cherry-red spot, hemorrhage, or peripheral neovascularization was present.

- Fluorescein angiography (left eye): Normal cilioretinal, retinal arteriolar, and retinal venous filling; abnormal retinal capillary bed across the macula, with increased intercapillary spacing and small areas of hypofluorescence nasal to the fovea.- OCT (left eye): Hyperreflective plaques at the level of the INL/OPL, corresponding to ophthalmoscopically opaque areas.  Image Title: Figure 1. Fundus Photograph at Presentation and Corresponding OCT Images  Image Description: Patient's fundus examination findings showing retinal atrophy  Image Title: Figure 2. OCT Collage Image  Image Description: Foveal scan at outcome vs scan of healthy age-matched person, demonstrating atrophy of middle retinal layers- OCT (right eye): Temporal macular thinning.

root.label: Subacute Unilateral Visual Loss with Ischemic Macular Changes
supporting_facts: 2-day history of visual loss in the left eye
ischemic macular whitening in the left eye
abnormal retinal capillary bed on fluorescein angiography
excluded_candidates: Optic neuritis: less likely given the absence of pain and the presence of ischemic macular changes
Central retinal artery occlusion: less likely given the normal retinal arteriolar filling on fluorescein angiography
salient_findings: abnormal retinal capillary bed on fluorescein angiography
hyperreflective plaques at the level of the INL/OPL on OCT
